title: wien2wannier 3.0: hybrid pre-Wannierization for WIEN2k

creators.name: Comaskey, William P.
creators.affiliation: Department of Mathematics, University of Nevada, Las Vegas

creators.name: Mendoza-Cortes, Jose L.
creators.affiliation: Department of Chemical Engineering & Materials Science and Department of Physics and Astronomy, Michigan State University

description:
wien2wannier 3.0 is a modified version of wien2wannier, the interface between WIEN2k and Wannier90. From a completed WIEN2k calculation, including spin-polarized and spin–orbit cases, it writes the projections, overlaps and band energies that Wannier90 reads.

Version 3.0 adds a hybrid pre-Wannierization, which freezes every Bloch state below an energy ceiling. Given the number of Wannier functions, the program can lower this ceiling from 8 eV above the Fermi energy until no k-point has more states below it than there are Wannier functions. With the frozen states held fixed, it minimizes the gauge-invariant spread, builds an SCDM gauge and writes Wannier90 input for an isolated set of bands, as many as there are Wannier functions. A second route writes the same selection as Wannier90 disentanglement windows.

Version 3.0 was developed and tested with WIEN2k 24.1, which it does not include. Installed into WIEN2k, it replaces only the programs w2w and w2wc and adds the program w2w_hybrid and a driver. The release has a user guide with a worked GaAs example and scripts that plot the projectability diagnostics of each run. The driver needs Python 3.10 or newer, and building needs a Fortran compiler, BLAS and LAPACK.

It is distributed under the GNU GPL, version 3 or later, and builds on wien2wannier 2.0 by J. Kuneš, P. Wissgott, E. Assmann and others. Its license requires every publication that uses it to cite J. Kuneš et al., Comput. Phys. Commun. 181, 1888 (2010). Please also cite W. P. Comaskey and J. L. Mendoza-Cortes, "Fully Automated Wannier Disentanglement via Projectability Selection in Gaussian and Augmented Plane-Wave Frameworks" (2026, in preparation). The calculations of the paper are archived at doi:10.5281/zenodo.23485290.
